title: A fair conclusion allows another perspective

captions.physics: Comparing observations in a clear sequence
captions.energy: Seeking a fair basis for judgement

meaning: Careful comparison can help you form a fair shared view while allowing time to absorb a change in an earlier assessment.
text: An earlier assessment can pause before a fresh certainty takes its place. The Emperor in the physical position of Ajna suggests comparing observations stepwise and distinguishing fact from conclusion. Justice in energy supports a search for fair foundations and proportion in relation to the known material. The Hanged Man in emotions experiences a pause while another perspective becomes possible. You may need time for a familiar judgement to stop directing discussion.

For example, you discuss a message about an upcoming gathering and initially hear a firm promise in it. Separating its exact words from your expectation reveals the phrase “we’ll try to come”. **A fair assessment can begin with a pause in a familiar judgement.** What the message actually gave you reason to expect becomes clearer. Adjusting the inner feeling immediately may be difficult because certainty already entered the conversation. Fresh understanding nevertheless has a clear foundation you can name without further guesses about someone else’s intentions.

The difficulty is remaining in reconsideration so long that a clear distinction stops helping. You discuss the initial expectation again as though it needs a final verdict. Proportion can apply to the examination itself. One accurate distinction may suffice for this phrase; an emotional pause need not become an endless investigation of the same message.
